html:
Full marks: 100. Time: 2 hours. Choose the best answer. Each question carries one mark and no negative marking is reported, so answer every question. How to score yourself: marks = number right.

This paper's question counts
Group Part Questions
A English (1–40) vocabulary 6, idioms and prepositions 6, articles/tenses/agreement 7, voice/narration/tags 5, clauses/conditionals 6, pronouns/modals 5, reading 5 40
B Mathematics (41–90) arithmetic 10, algebra 10, trigonometry 4, coordinate geometry 7, vectors 2, calculus 7, reasoning 10 50
C GK and IT (91–100) Nepal 3, world 2, computer 3, Internet/programming 2 10

Read the passage and answer questions 36–40.

Kathmandu's old bazaars have sold spices, cloth and brass for centuries, and many shopkeepers are the fourth or fifth generation of their families to sit behind the same counter.

Today they compete with online stores, yet the bazaars survive because customers trust a seller they know. A trader who remembers what you bought last Dashain, and gives honest advice, offers something a website cannot easily copy.

Some shops now take digital payments while keeping the old way of talking over tea.

  4. The word "compete" meansacooperatebcopycretiredtry to win against
  5. Which item is NOT mentioned in the passage?agoldbclothcspicesdbrass

2.4 Answer key and explanations

Answers — Group A English (1–40)

1. (b) — ample means plentiful.

2. (a) — rigid is stiff; flexible is the opposite.

3. (c) — polyglot; bilingual is two languages.

4. (d) — tranquil means calm.

5. (a) — extempore.

6. (c) — arrogant is proud; humble is the opposite.

7. (b) — to joke with someone.

8. (d) — insist on.

9. (a) — give in means surrender.

10. (c) — allergic to.

11. (b) — a fuss over something trivial.

12. (d) — look into means investigate.

13. (c) — "one-eyed" begins with a "w" sound, so a.

14. (b) — "for ten years": present perfect.

15. (a) — a distance treated as one unit takes a singular verb.

16. (d) — the train left before I reached: past perfect.

17. (b) — the nearer subject, students, is plural.

18. (c) — "since 2019": present perfect.

19. (a) — "each" takes a singular verb.

20. (b) — simple past passive.

21. (c) — am becomes was.

22. (b) — "never" is negative, so a positive tag.

23. (a) — wh-question in statement order.

24. (c) — present continuous passive.

25. (c) — possession: whose.

26. (a) — second conditional: would.

27. (d) — suggest + -ing.

28. (c) — have something done.

29. (a) — "unless" already negates; the main clause is "won't".

30. (d) — make + bare verb.

31. (c) — "few" suggests loneliness, a negative sense.

32. (b) — senior to.

33. (a) — hardly … when.

34. (c) — prohibition.

35. (b) — advice is uncountable.

36. (b) — the trust-based survival of the bazaars.

37. (c) — "fourth or fifth generation".

38. (a) — "remembers what you bought … honest advice".

39. (d) — compete means try to win against.

40. (a) — gold is not mentioned.

2.5 Score sheet and error analysis

Use the figures and steps below after you finish the paper. Mark your sheet with the answer key, enter the group scores, then work through the error log.

  1. Score each group separately and compare with the target boxes in Fig 2.2. A low group tells you which units to revisit first.
  2. Write an error log line for every miss: question number, the cause (formula, arithmetic slip, grammar rule, never learnt) and the unit that fixes it.
  3. Redo each missed question after two days, without looking at the explanation. A question you can now solve is fixed; one you cannot goes back into the log.
  4. Check your time: if Mathematics took more than 70 minutes, practise skipping and returning (Fig 2.2).
  5. Do not read patterns into the key (Fig 2.1). The letters are spread across a, b, c and d.
